problem.text: MixtralForCausalLM needs an architecture-specific configuration and checkpoint mapping before Config.from_directory can select it.

reasoning.text: The change reuses existing attention, transformer-block and sparse-expert implementations rather than introducing Mixtral-specific kernels.

impact.text: Registers MixtralModel and supplies MixtralConfig, making the architecture selectable through the existing configuration factory.

source_notes.text: Issue #7, “quantizing model: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate,” reports a native-extension import failure and the reporter's environment workaround. Its connection here is only inferred from the traceback's config.py import line; it is not evidence of a Mixtral defect or motivation for this change.
PR #4, “chore: update config.py,” proposes “containg → containing.” Its inferred connection is the matching typo in the shared configuration source, not architecture support.

limitations: No model loading, conversion, generation or GPU execution was performed. The Python calculation checks transcribed shape arithmetic only.
Checkpoint tensor headers were not inspected; configuration compatibility does not establish that every weight is loadable or numerical outputs match a reference implementation.

claims.text: MixtralConfig reads intermediate_size into moe_intermediate_size and num_local_experts into num_experts. These are deliberate checkpoint-key mappings: the existing Qwen3 MoE configuration instead reads moe_intermediate_size and num_experts. num_experts_per_tok controls how many experts are selected.

Missing or false-valued head_dim is derived as hidden_size // num_attention_heads; absent KV-head count defaults to the query-head count. hidden_act may be absent but must equal silu when supplied. The model uses NEOX-style RoPE settings and defaults tied embeddings to false.

Assembly is embedding → repeated pre-normalized attention and MoE residual blocks → final RMSNorm → vocabulary projection. Attention maps q_proj/k_proj/v_proj/o_proj. Each block_sparse_moe maps expert w1 to the activation gate, w3 to the up projection and w2 to the down projection; gate is the separate router. Expert intermediates and outputs are explicitly half precision.

The reused router produces unpadded expert scores, applies softmax, selects top-k experts and renormalizes their weights. Multiple flattened tokens or non-fully-EXL3 experts use the per-expert Torch path; a single token with fully EXL3 experts uses indexed fused projections. MultiLinear additionally requires compatible dimensions and K, no bias or softcap, and unit post-scale.

prepare_inputs preserves input_ids in params and delegates attention preparation. The shared default is uncached Flash Attention; SDPA and cached Flash Attention remain explicit alternatives with their existing cache and shape requirements. Mixtral supplies no sliding-window override.

The pinned mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-v0.1 and Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 configurations each match the new configuration mapping: hidden size 4096, intermediate size 14336, 32 layers, 32 query heads, eight KV heads and vocabulary 32000. Both specify eight experts with two selected per token.

The pinned mistralai/Mixtral-8x22B-v0.1 matches with hidden size 6144, intermediate size 16384, 56 layers, 48 query heads, eight KV heads and vocabulary 32000. Mixtral-8x22B-Instruct-v0.1 has the same dimensions except vocabulary 32768. Both likewise specify eight experts and top-two routing.

All four configurations omit head_dim, specify silu, untied embeddings, RMS epsilon 1e-5 and null sliding_window. They supply rope_theta 1000000 rather than using the shared 10000 fallback. Their declared bfloat16 dtype does not change this adapter's explicit half-precision MoE intermediates.

A standard-library calculation of the inspected dimension formulas gives head dimension 128 and KV projection width 1024 for all four models. Query-head grouping is four per KV head for 8x7B and six for 8x22B; assembled top-level module counts are respectively 35 and 59.

annotation.summary: Adds Mixtral registration and configuration-to-module mappings, reusing existing grouped-query attention and sparse-expert execution. Four pinned model configurations match the adapter's principal dimensions and defaults; runtime compatibility remains untested.

argv:
import json
for name,h,q,kv,i,l,v in [('8x7B',4096,32,8,14336,32,32000),('8x7B-Instruct',4096,32,8,14336,32,32000),('8x22B',6144,48,8,16384,56,32000),('8x22B-Instruct',6144,48,8,16384,56,32768)]:
 d=h//q
 print(json.dumps(dict(model=name,head_dim=d,q_width=q*d,kv_width=kv*d,q_per_kv=q//kv,modules=l+3,expert_up_shape=[i,h],expert_down_shape=[h,i],head_shape=[v,h])))
